title: BWH eSign native field definition document, version 1.1
description: The one versioned field schema shared by the visual editor and the native API (docs/HANDOFF.md section 7, docs/preparation/field-schema.md). Rectangles are stored in the native coordinate space as plain numbers; converting them to PDF user space is the job of App\Domain\Preparation\Geometry, never of this document. This file is the contract: the PHP importer, the TypeScript editor types, and the fixtures are all validated against it.

schema_version.description: Exact version of this contract. An importer refuses an unknown major version outright and refuses a minor version it does not implement; it never guesses. 1.1 adds the optional anchor members `placement`, `required`, `tolerance` and the service-written `resolved` receipt; a document that uses none of them is a 1.0 document and says so, and this build reads both.

document_id.description: Stable identifier of the prepared document this field set belongs to.

recipients.description: Every recipient referenced by a field or by the signing order. Order is not significant; signing_order carries the sequence.

signing_order.description: Sequential stages of parallel recipients. [["a"],["b"]] signs a then b; [["a","b"]] signs both in parallel. Every recipient appears exactly once, in exactly one stage.

fields.description: The field definitions. May be empty while a document is still being prepared; the send-time gate, not this schema, requires at least one field.

identifier.description: A stable, caller-chosen identifier. Preserved byte-for-byte across import and export so field ids and template aliases survive a round trip.

coordinate_space.description: The declared coordinate space. Version 1.0 implements exactly one, and every value is a const: a document that declares anything else is rejected rather than reinterpreted. Never infer points versus percent from a number's magnitude.

origin.description: Origin at the top-left of the displayed page box, y growing downwards.

page_box.description: Coordinates are relative to the CropBox clipped to the MediaBox, which is what a viewer displays.

rotation.description: Coordinates are in the displayed (post-/Rotate) orientation.

role.description: Optional display label for the party ("Buyer", "Witness"). Carries no authority: it is not an application role and grants nothing.

allOf.$comment: anchor.required false means an absent anchor omits the field, and a required field cannot be omitted. Both importers refuse the combination as anchor_optional_on_required_field, so the published contract refuses it too rather than telling a client its document conforms and letting the service answer 422. `required` defaults to true, so the field has to say false explicitly.

id.description: Stable field id, unique within the document.

recipient_id.description: Must match the id of a recipient in this document.

page.description: 1-based page number in the prepared document.

required.description: Whether the recipient must complete the field. Omitted means true: an unstated requirement fails closed.

read_only.description: Whether the recipient may edit the value. Omitted means false.

label.description: Optional human-readable label shown in the editor and to the signer.

alias.description: Optional stable template alias for the field, unique within the document. Templates address fields by alias so a re-prepared document keeps its mapping.

field_type.description: The field types version 1.0 implements. Any further control is a declared capability in a later version, never a silently ignored member of this list.

rect.description: An axis-aligned rectangle in the declared coordinate space, anchored at its top-left corner. Values are finite, carry at most three decimal places (0.001 pt), and are written without a trailing fractional zero when integral.

measured_rect.description: A rectangle recording where something was, rather than where something goes. Same unit, orientation and canonical spelling as rect, but x and y may be negative and nothing is checked against the page edge — see resolved_anchor.anchor_rect. Only the extents are constrained, to being non-negative, because a box with a negative extent is not a measurement of anything.

prefill.description: Binds the field's initial value to a named variable resolved at send time. An unresolved variable is an error before send, never a blank field.

anchor.description: An anchor placement request: find this text, then place the field's rect relative to it, or check the rect that is already there. Resolution is deterministic positioned-text extraction (App\Domain\Preparation\Text) that writes the resolved rectangle and a receipt back into this document when a template version is published and again when an envelope is sent, and never after that; a missing or ambiguous required anchor is an error, never a guess. Matching semantics belong to the resolver, not to this schema. See docs/preparation/field-schema.md.

allOf.$comment: tolerance is the slack a cross_check is judged against. In replace mode the anchor decides the position outright, so there is no declared rectangle for a tolerance to be measured from.

required false means an absent anchor omits the field; in cross_check the declared rectangle is authoritative and the anchor only checks it, so an absent anchor has nothing to omit. placement defaults to replace, so an omitted placement satisfies this.

A cross_check receipt is the record of a comparison, and the standard it was judged against belongs in the document. Without a stated tolerance the receipt's claim would have to be re-derived from whatever the deployment happens to be configured with later.

text.description: Exact text to locate. Matched case-sensitively against decoded text runs; never a regular expression over PDF bytes and never a fuzzy match.

occurrence.description: Which match to place against: "sole" means the text must occur exactly once in scope, an integer is a 1-based index in document order. Required, with no default: an anchor that matches twice without saying which one it means is under-specified, and silently taking the first would move a signature box the moment the contract text changes. The resolver's "all" mode places one box per match, which a single field cannot represent, so it is not a value here.

placement.description: Which of the field's two statements about position wins. "replace" makes the anchor authoritative for x and y and keeps only the rect's width and height, because an anchor says where a field goes and never how big it is; the rect's x and y are then a placeholder that resolution overwrites, and nothing is ever left at it. "cross_check" keeps the declared rect and requires the anchor to resolve within `tolerance` points of it, which is the mode for a document whose layout the consumer generates itself. Omitted means "replace": that is the only behaviour an anchor in this schema has ever had, so it is what an already-written document meant, and a canonical form that added the property would move the field-schema digest every attestation on an anchored agreement is bound to.

origin.description: Corner of the matched text box the offset is measured from. Omitted means top-left; nothing is inferred from the sign of the offset.

offset.description: Offset from the origin corner, in the same unit and orientation as the coordinate space, so dy grows downwards. May be negative.

required.description: Whether the anchor text must be present. Omitted means true: an unstated requirement fails closed. False is the narrow compatibility option for a document in which this text may legitimately not appear — the field is then omitted from the sent envelope rather than placed anywhere, and the omission is recorded on the envelope. Only accepted on a field whose own `required` is false and whose placement is "replace", and it never makes an ambiguous anchor acceptable.

tolerance.description: How far, in points, a "cross_check" anchor may resolve from the declared rect before the disagreement is an error. Omitted takes the deployment default (esign.preparation.anchor_cross_check_tolerance). Meaningless, and rejected, with placement "replace". Bounded by PDF's largest page side, 14400 pt: a tolerance is a distance between two positions on one page, so nothing beyond that can mean anything here. The bound is there to keep the canonical form total rather than because a larger number would be unreasonable — above roughly 1e20 this schema's two implementations spell the same value differently (PHP writes 1.0e+20 where JavaScript writes 100000000000000000000), so such a document would canonicalise to two different digests, and field_schema_sha256 is what every attestation binds.

resolved_anchor.description: What resolution found, written by the service and never by a caller authoring a document. The anchor is the question, the field's rect is the answer everything downstream uses, and this is the receipt in between. `document_sha256` is the digest of the exact bytes the text was located in: provenance for a stored rectangle, not a reason to skip re-measuring it. Publishing a template version and sending an envelope each resolve every anchored field again, receipt or no receipt, because a receipt is bound to a document, a page and an occurrence but not to the anchor text, origin or offset. Sending therefore always reads the document. After send nothing re-resolves at all.

document_sha256.description: SHA-256, lowercase hex, of the document revision the text was located in.

page.description: 1-based page the match was found on. Equal to the field's own page: an anchor is searched on the page the field declares.

occurrence_index.description: 1-based index, in deterministic document order, of the match that was taken.

anchor_rect.description: Where the matched text itself sits. A measurement, not a placement: a run's nominal box is its advance by the font's ascent plus descent, so a heading near the top of the page legitimately starts above the CropBox edge and a run at the margin legitimately ends on it. Never checked against the page.

rect.description: The rectangle resolution produced: the anchor rect's chosen corner plus the offset, sized by the field. In "replace" mode this is required to be the field's own rect, so the receipt cannot describe a placement that did not happen.
